business_model.claim: Trinity reports two segments: the Railcar Leasing and Services Group and the Rail Products Group.
quotes: We report our operating results in two reportable segments: (1) the Railcar Leasing and Services Group (the "Leasing Group"), which owns and operates a fleet of railcars and provides third-party fleet leasing, management, and administrative services; railcar maintenance and modification services; and other railcar logistics products and services; and (2) the Rail Products Group, which manufactures and sells railcars and related parts and components.

business_model.claim: The Leasing Group earns revenue primarily from full-service operating leases of freight and tank railcars to industrial shippers and railroads, with fixed monthly rentals of one to ten years.
quotes: we primarily offer full-service operating leases for freight and tank railcars
The railcars in our lease fleet are leased to industrial shippers and railroads.
The terms of our railcar leases generally provide for fixed monthly rentals that vary from one year to ten years.

business_model.claim: The Rail Products Group manufactures freight and tank railcars in the U.S. and Mexico and sells them to railroads, leasing companies, and industrial shippers.
quotes: Through wholly-owned subsidiaries with facilities in the U.S. and Mexico, our Rail Products Group is a leading manufacturer of freight and tank railcars in North America used for transporting a wide variety of liquids, gases, and dry cargo.

Our customers include railroads, leasing companies, and industrial shippers of products in various markets, such as refined products and chemicals, energy, agriculture, construction and metals, and consumer products.

business_model.claim: Substantially all railcars in the Leasing Group's fleet were manufactured by the Rail Products Group, creating an internal supply chain between the two segments.
quotes: Substantially all of the railcars in our lease fleet were manufactured by our Rail Products Group.
New railcars | $434.0 | $461.4

business_model.claim: The company also generates revenue from railcar maintenance and modifications, parts and components, and digital and logistics services under the RSI Logistics brand.
quotes: Our platform provides railcar leasing and management services; railcar manufacturing; railcar maintenance and modifications; and other railcar logistics products and services.
Our platform also includes the brands of RSI Logistics, a provider of software and logistics solutions, and Holden America, a supplier of railcar parts and components.

business_model.claim: Leasing Group revenue is driven by lease rates, net fleet additions, and fleet utilization; in 2025 leasing and management revenues rose 5.9% primarily due to higher lease rates and net additions to the lease fleet.
quotes: Leasing and management revenues increased by 5.9% for the year ended December 31, 2025 when compared to the prior year primarily due to higher lease rates and net additions to the lease fleet.

business_model.claim: Rail Products Group revenue is driven primarily by railcar delivery volumes; in 2025 revenues fell 41.6% and cost of revenues fell 40.7% primarily due to lower deliveries.
quotes: Revenues and cost of revenues for the Rail Products Group decreased for the year ended December 31, 2025 by 41.6% and 40.7%, respectively, when compared to the prior year primarily due to lower deliveries.

business_model.claim: Steel and other raw materials represent more than 70% of the cost of most railcars, making input cost volatility a primary cost driver for the Rail Products Group.

competitive_position.claim: Trinity has experienced shortages of skilled labor, particularly welders, and increased turnover at certain facilities, which restricts production rates and increases labor costs.

competitive_position.claim: Trinity's profitability depends on its ability to re-lease or sell railcars at satisfactory rates; a downturn in lessee industries could increase re-marketing risk and reduce lease utilization and rates.

A downturn in the industries in which our lessees operate and decreased demand for railcars could also increase our exposure to re-marketing risk because lessees may demand shorter lease terms or newer railcars.
